entry.hops: No wire in the Node test: the daemon client is the real session service called in process; replies are recorded as the objects returned (and their JSON byte size, a measure). A replay over the real daemon wire records the same reply objects.
entry.notRun: no real store or runtime; the viewer is one local client token
entry.runs: createSessionService (subscribeSession, readSession) with a scripted readStoredSession over 300 rows, SessionHostTransport.readSession, SessionHostPublication (projections, applySessionResult, applyTranscriptPage, heldTranscript), SessionTranscriptWindows

normalised.reason: per-run temp path (or generated name) replaced by a placeholder

product.tree: product tree loaded by the recorder

replay.compare: mixdog-app-server thread/items/list: replay the open and the next-page read; compare the read args the host sent, each reply whole (page/full, items, byte size) and the held snapshot whole
replay.entry: Drive thread/items/list (mixdog-core-session/src/session/reads.rs items_list) over a real store: mixdog-app-server-daemon session_host_replay_tests (an_older_page_answers_only_the_revealed_rows_as_node_recorded, a_session_that_changed_between_reads_shows_the_recorded_window_as_node_recorded, held_rows_that_move_during_a_page_read_fall_back_to_a_full_read_as_node_recorded).

normalised.rowIds: a row id is the core's item id where the recorder scripted c0..c299; the rows are compared whole without it
normalised.rowText: the recorder handed its scripted rows to the host untrimmed (`row <id> ` x50); a stored assistant message restores as its trimmed text in Node (transcript-restore/restore.mjs restoredAssistantTranscriptItems) and in the core alike, so the recorded text is compared trimmed
normalised.changedBetweenReads: a session that changed between reads: Node's host answered the newest 96 rows in full (session-service.mjs readSession, transcriptItemLimit). The Rust client pages by position (512 rows a page in production, the recorded 64 here), so the 98 rows it displays (older page 64 + held 32 + the 2 appended) are compared whole: the two rows beyond Node's window (the first two rows of the recorded older page), then the recorded 96. The client's own detection (TranscriptHistoryPager.earlier: the tail moved while the page was in flight, the page is dropped, the caller reads the window again) is replayed in apps/desktop/src/renderer/transcript-history-window.test.mjs against the recorded rows; the replacing read is the full read compared here
normalised.inFlightMovement: the held rows are the desktop host's own copy (session-host-publication.ts heldTranscript, digest check in session-service.mjs readSession): the core has no counterpart and the recorder changed only that copy. The Rust replay holds the page read before it reaches the store (CallCounted::hold on history_rows), drops the first row of the client's held copy as the recorder did, releases the read and compares the page it answered and the full read whole with the recorded reads[0] and reads[1]. The client's detection and fallback (the held rows moved: the page is dropped and the window read again) are TranscriptHistoryPager.earlier, replayed in apps/desktop/src/renderer/transcript-history-window.test.mjs
normalised.pageShape: Node's host reply wrapper (page/full, projectionStamp, byte size) is the desktop host's; the core answers the same rows and hasOlder on thread/items/list (older page by the opening page's nextCursor; full read without a cursor)
